title: Behavioral UX Contract
description: One object per PERSUASIVE or HIGH-RISK behavioral intervention. Forces a declared hypothesis, evidence grade, user benefit, and risk before implementation. See references/14-behavioral-ux.md.

surface.description: Where this intervention lives (e.g. onboarding, pricing, upgrade, renewal, cancellation).

hypothesis.description: A falsifiable behavioral hypothesis, not a command (e.g. 'showing real completed steps improves orientation and completion', never 'use loss aversion here').

evidenceGrade.description: A: strong replicated/meta-analytic evidence. B: good, context-dependent. C: limited/indirect. D: practitioner heuristic/product precedent only.

userBenefit.description: Must be completable honestly: 'this helps the user by ___'. Never left generic/empty.

truthful.description: Always true — a Behavioral UX Contract for a deceptive intervention is a contradiction; deceptive patterns are handled under prohibited-patterns, not this contract.

reversible.description: Whether the user can undo/change the outcome this intervention nudges toward.

userControl.description: 'reduced' requires manipulationRisk to be at least 'high' and a written justification in notes.

experimentRequired.description: True unless the surface has no measurable traffic — see references/14-behavioral-ux.md and outcome-evidence.md for the qualitative fallback.

guardrails.description: Metrics that must not silently degrade while primaryMetric improves (e.g. setup-error-rate, support-contact-rate, early-churn, refund-rate).
